# QuilrAI Documentation

> QuilrAI governs how an enterprise uses AI: a Console to observe and set policy, an LLM Gateway and MCP Gateway in front of models and tools, a Browser Extension and Endpoint Agent on the workforce side, Red Teaming to test AI systems, and Integrations with the platforms you already run.

## Console

See every AI interaction across your organization, decide what is allowed, and prove it. The docs follow the console menu, so each page here matches a page there.

- [Console overview](https://docs.quilrai.dev/console.md): Landing page with the main tasks and every section of Console.

### Get started

- [Console tour](https://docs.quilrai.dev/console/get-started/console-tour.md): The QuilrAI console at web.quilr.ai is organised around what you manage (people, applications, agents, interactions and controls), not around the sensors that collect the data. This page shows how the sidebar is laid...
- [Views, filters and drawers](https://docs.quilrai.dev/console/get-started/views-filters-and-drawers.md): Most console pages share the same controls. Learn them once and they work the same way on Findings & Interactions, Users, Inventory, Agents, Costs & Savings and the other list pages.
- [Moving from Console V1](https://docs.quilrai.dev/console/get-started/moving-from-console-v1.md): Ground rules, the three transition phases, and where to do what while both consoles run in parallel.

### Observe

- [Overview](https://docs.quilrai.dev/console/observe/overview.md): Overview is the executive snapshot of how your organisation uses AI, what agentic assets exist, and where risk stands. Open it from Observe > Overview. It has three tabs, and the period selector at the top (for...
- [Costs & Savings](https://docs.quilrai.dev/console/observe/costs-and-savings.md): Costs & Savings shows what your organisation spends on AI, how many tokens it uses, how many tokens Quilr already saves, and which settings would save more. Open it from Observe > Costs & Savings.
- [Graph](https://docs.quilrai.dev/console/observe/graph.md): Graph shows how people, applications, agents, MCP servers, data and controls connect, as an interactive map. Open it from Observe > Graph. Use it to answer questions such as "which agents reach this MCP server?" or...
- [Findings & Interactions](https://docs.quilrai.dev/console/observe/findings-and-interactions.md): Findings & Interactions is the one place to see what people did with AI and what Quilr flagged along the way. Open it from Observe > Findings & Interactions in the sidebar.
- [Triage center](https://docs.quilrai.dev/console/observe/triage-center.md): The Triage center is where you work the findings queue. It helps you close findings that no longer need action, see who changed what, set up rules for new findings, and tune detections so the same false positives...
- [Users](https://docs.quilrai.dev/console/observe/users.md): Users shows each person's AI usage and risk, and how well Quilr's sensors cover them. Open it from Observe > Users. The page has five tabs: All users, Browser deployment, Endpoint deployment, Accounts and Quilly.
- [Inventory](https://docs.quilrai.dev/console/observe/inventory.md): Inventory is the catalog of every AI asset Quilr has discovered: applications, browser extensions, AI clients, models, MCP servers, agents, skills, plugins, hooks, repositories and more. Open it from Observe > Inventory.
- [Agents](https://docs.quilrai.dev/console/observe/agents.md): Agents lists every AI agent observed across your estate, and the skills, MCP servers, system prompts, models and people behind each one. Open it from Observe > Agents.
- [Dashboards](https://docs.quilrai.dev/console/observe/dashboards.md): Dashboards lets you build custom dashboards by describing them in plain language to an AI designer. Open it from Observe > Dashboards (the page is titled Custom dashboards).

### Govern

- [Policy Engine overview](https://docs.quilrai.dev/console/govern/policy-engine.md): The Policy Engine decides what happens when AI use crosses a line. It has one tab per enforcement surface, and each surface holds the controls enforced through that product.
- [Author, simulate and publish](https://docs.quilrai.dev/console/govern/author-simulate-and-publish.md): The draft, validate, simulate, replay, publish and roll back loop, plus permissions and engine limits.
- [Switching from classic settings](https://docs.quilrai.dev/console/govern/switching-from-classic-settings.md): The conversion review, what each target's conversion compares, activation, which settings freeze, and a recommended first rollout.
- [Detection Models](https://docs.quilrai.dev/console/govern/detection-models.md): Detection Models define what counts as sensitive data or an adversarial prompt. Policies and controls refer to these detections by name, so this page is where you decide what Quilr looks for, and how risky each...
- [Custom detections and library](https://docs.quilrai.dev/console/govern/custom-detections-and-library.md): When the built-in Detection Models do not cover what you need caught, such as an internal project codename, a customer ID format or a topic you want to keep out of AI tools, add a custom detection model. You can...
- [Action requests](https://docs.quilrai.dev/console/govern/action-requests.md): When a browser extension control stops a user from doing something, such as uploading a file or visiting a site, the user can submit a justification and ask for the action to be allowed. Those requests land here for...

### Settings · AI Gateway

- [Skills Library](https://docs.quilrai.dev/console/settings-ai-gateway/skills-library.md): Agent Skills are packaged instructions and tools that AI coding agents and assistants load on demand. The Skills Library lets you discover the skills already in use on your endpoints, vet skills from pinned public...
- [Workflow Agents](https://docs.quilrai.dev/console/settings-ai-gateway/workflow-agents.md): Workflow Agents lets you build and run AI agents connected to your tools. Each agent combines a model, a set of tools and an engine.

### Settings · Organization

- [General and domains](https://docs.quilrai.dev/console/settings-organization/general-and-domains.md): The General page holds your organization's identity and decides what happens when users browse from a browser your organization does not manage.
- [Smart Groups](https://docs.quilrai.dev/console/settings-organization/smart-groups.md): Smart Groups are named sets of people that you reuse across the console: in Policy Engine conditions, browser and endpoint controls, and access assignments in Roles and permissions.
- [Roles and permissions](https://docs.quilrai.dev/console/settings-organization/roles-and-permissions.md): Roles and permissions control who can open which console pages and which data they see. Access is defined by one versioned access policy: roles hold permissions, and people and Smart Groups hold roles.
- [Single sign-on](https://docs.quilrai.dev/console/settings-organization/single-sign-on.md): Connect a SAML identity provider (IdP) so admins sign in to the console through your IdP.
- [Organizational policies](https://docs.quilrai.dev/console/settings-organization/organizational-policies.md): Upload your written policies, such as an AI acceptable-use policy, so Quilr can cite them in controls, detections and the guidance users see when Quilr intervenes.
- [Data sources](https://docs.quilrai.dev/console/settings-organization/data-sources.md): Choose which sensors and integrations feed data into the console views.
- [Audit logs](https://docs.quilrai.dev/console/settings-organization/audit-logs.md): The audit log records who changed or accessed what in the console, and when. Use it for change review, incident investigation and compliance evidence.

### Settings · Data

- [Data retention](https://docs.quilrai.dev/console/settings-data/data-retention.md): Data Retention sets how long LLM Gateway and MCP Gateway data stays visible in the console. You set a default horizon for each kind of data, then add ordered rules for traffic that needs a different horizon.
- [Export Center](https://docs.quilrai.dev/console/settings-data/export-center.md): One place to create, schedule and download exports of console data.

### Settings · Sensors and more

- [End-user popups](https://docs.quilrai.dev/console/settings-sensors/end-user-popups.md): When Quilr intervenes, for example to coach a user, ask for a justification or block an action, the user sees a popup. The User Interaction Hub controls how those popups look and what they say.
- [Display and profile](https://docs.quilrai.dev/console/settings-sensors/display-and-profile.md): Two small settings pages: Display for presentation preferences, and User Profile for your own account details.

### Console V1 (legacy)

- [Console V1 Administrator Guide](https://docs.quilrai.dev/console/legacy-v1/overview.md): Reading paths for deployment, administration, governance, investigations, and reporting in Console V1.

#### Administration

- [Settings Overview](https://docs.quilrai.dev/console/legacy-v1/administration/settings.md): Console V1 settings areas, save behavior, responsibilities, and audit verification.
- [Organizational Context](https://docs.quilrai.dev/console/legacy-v1/administration/organizational-context.md): Configure organization identity, corporate domains, timezone, acceptable-use policies, profile, and unmanaged-browser behavior.
- [Console Access Control](https://docs.quilrai.dev/console/legacy-v1/administration/access-control.md): Manage console invitations, groups, and the six console roles through Manage Users.
- [User Interaction Hub](https://docs.quilrai.dev/console/legacy-v1/administration/user-interaction-hub.md): Customize prompt branding, message templates, justification options, and policy links for end users.

#### Policies and Detections

- [Policy Configuration and Lifecycle](https://docs.quilrai.dev/console/legacy-v1/policies-and-detections/policy-lifecycle.md): Create, scope, test, promote, maintain, duplicate, and disable browser and endpoint controls.
- [Detection Models](https://docs.quilrai.dev/console/legacy-v1/policies-and-detections/detection-models.md): Review contextual and pattern-based models, test synthetic samples, and validate custom detections.

#### Inventory and Investigations

- [AI Assets](https://docs.quilrai.dev/console/legacy-v1/investigations/ai-assets.md): Inspect endpoint and SaaS AI inventory, asset fields, usage, guardrails, and investigation pivots.
- [Users and Accounts](https://docs.quilrai.dev/console/legacy-v1/investigations/users-and-accounts.md): Distinguish people from application accounts and correlate identity, login context, and findings.
- [Findings and Investigations](https://docs.quilrai.dev/console/legacy-v1/investigations/findings.md): Triage browser and endpoint findings, interpret outcomes, correlate evidence, and manage disposition.
- [End-to-End Investigation Workflow](https://docs.quilrai.dev/console/legacy-v1/investigations/end-to-end-workflow.md): Trace a sensitive-data signal through findings, identities, AI assets, controls, audit history, and exports.

#### Reporting and Audit

- [Dashboards and Exports](https://docs.quilrai.dev/console/legacy-v1/reporting/dashboards-and-exports.md): Interpret time-bounded dashboards, export filtered CSV evidence, and manage the central export queue.
- [Audit Logging Console](https://docs.quilrai.dev/console/legacy-v1/reporting/audit-log.md): Attribute administrative changes, filter audit events, configure columns, and export audit evidence.
- [Insights and Governance Reports](https://docs.quilrai.dev/console/legacy-v1/reporting/insights-and-governance-reports.md): Review adoption, sensitive-data trends, governance incidents, and executive summaries with evidence drill-downs.
- [Troubleshooting and Completion Checklist](https://docs.quilrai.dev/console/legacy-v1/troubleshooting.md): Diagnose deployment, telemetry, policy, and export issues; locate logs and confirm operational readiness.

## LLM Gateway

Point your apps at one OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Every request gets guardrails, routing, limits and cost tracking, whichever provider serves it.

- [LLM Gateway overview](https://docs.quilrai.dev/llm-gateway.md): Landing page with the main tasks and every section of LLM Gateway.

### Get started

- [LLM Gateway overview](https://docs.quilrai.dev/llm-gateway/get-started/overview.md): What the gateway is, apps vs Quilr keys vs providers, and a tour of the console (overview cards, app workspace tabs, settings sections, self-service usage).
- [Quick Start](https://docs.quilrai.dev/llm-gateway/get-started/quick-start.md): Create an app in the console (platform providers or app-only credentials, guardrail defaults), send a first request, and check Activity.
- [Architecture](https://docs.quilrai.dev/llm-gateway/get-started/architecture.md): Request processing pipeline - Validate, Scan, Transform, Route - with a visual diagram of every stage.
- [Integration Guide](https://docs.quilrai.dev/llm-gateway/get-started/integration-guide.md): Endpoint URLs, authentication setup, and code examples for connecting your app to the gateway, including OpenAI-compatible access to Bedrock Converse, Vertex AI Gemini, and Anthropic Messages models, boto3 Bedrock Runtime, Sarvam speech and text, and Copilot Studio.
- [HA & SLA](https://docs.quilrai.dev/llm-gateway/get-started/ha-and-sla.md): Regional endpoints, recommended retry strategy, connection pooling, and 99.6% uptime SLA.

### Apps and providers

- [Applications and Keys](https://docs.quilrai.dev/llm-gateway/apps-and-providers/applications-and-keys.md): App naming and status, multiple named Quilr keys with expiry and revocation, log keys, API integration, configuration versions and rollback, and the app audit tab.
- [Providers and models](https://docs.quilrai.dev/llm-gateway/apps-and-providers/providers-and-models.md): Settings > AI Gateway > Models, platform providers and credential reuse across apps are available in the V2 console only. In V1, each app keeps its own provider credentials. :::
- [Provider Support](https://docs.quilrai.dev/llm-gateway/apps-and-providers/provider-support.md): Supported LLM providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Azure, Bedrock, Vertex AI, Oracle OCI, Sarvam, Copilot Studio) and their capability matrix with credentials per provider (incl. Oracle OCI auth modes, rerank, embeddings, Realtime, Assistants), including Oracle gateway sign-in, provider-native models through OpenAI-compatible endpoints, and the Sarvam speech and text APIs.
- [AWS Bedrock](https://docs.quilrai.dev/llm-gateway/apps-and-providers/aws-bedrock.md): Connect AWS Bedrock to the LLM Gateway with an IAM role instead of long-lived access keys, and call Bedrock through the gateway with boto3. Applies to the bedrock, anthropicmessagesbedrock, bedrockembeddings and...
- [Oracle OCI](https://docs.quilrai.dev/llm-gateway/apps-and-providers/oracle-oci.md): Grant QuilrAI cross-tenancy access to OCI Generative AI for Chat Completions and Responses without sharing an Oracle API key or signing key.
- [SDK Mode](https://docs.quilrai.dev/llm-gateway/apps-and-providers/sdk-mode.md): Scan text, messages, or structured JSON directly from application code. Documents hashing_mode, processed_json, JSON Pointer locations, placeholder mappings, and advisory similar_entities.

### Protect

- [Security guardrails](https://docs.quilrai.dev/llm-gateway/protect/security-guardrails.md): Detect sensitive data and adversarial input in prompts and responses, then monitor, redact or block it. Set the basics per app in the app's settings; use the Policy Engine's Data & Adversarial Risks card when you...
- [Custom detections](https://docs.quilrai.dev/llm-gateway/protect/custom-detections.md): Define your own detections - precision (regex) patterns or intents trained with examples.
- [Guardian agent](https://docs.quilrai.dev/llm-gateway/protect/guardian-agent.md): Guide model behavior with gateway checks for dependency safety and task adherence.
- [Hallucination protection](https://docs.quilrai.dev/llm-gateway/protect/hallucination-protection.md): V2 console Policy Engine card - Response confidence threshold and what happens after a hallucination is detected.
- [Identity and network trust](https://docs.quilrai.dev/llm-gateway/protect/identity-and-network-trust.md): Identify the user behind every gateway call, require identity or a conversation ID where you need it, verify caller JWTs, and limit which networks may call the gateway.
- [Gateway access and allowed models](https://docs.quilrai.dev/llm-gateway/protect/gateway-access-and-allowed-models.md): Control who may send requests through the gateway and which models they may call. Denied requests are rejected before routing or scanning: no provider call, no tokens.
- [Tool controls](https://docs.quilrai.dev/llm-gateway/protect/tool-controls.md): Allow or deny tool calls by tool name, declared annotations, wire type or argument values, independently of what data they carry.

### Cost and traffic

- [Routing and fallbacks](https://docs.quilrai.dev/llm-gateway/cost-and-traffic/routing-and-fallbacks.md): Spread one model name across several models, providers or accounts, fail over when a provider is down, and send small requests to cheaper models.
- [Rate, token and budget limits](https://docs.quilrai.dev/llm-gateway/cost-and-traffic/rate-token-and-budget-limits.md): Cap how long calls run, how many run at once, how many requests an app makes and how many tokens or dollars it spends. All limits are enforced at the gateway, before the request reaches the provider.
- [Token saving](https://docs.quilrai.dev/llm-gateway/cost-and-traffic/token-saving.md): Rewrite request content into fewer tokens before it reaches the provider. Responses are returned untouched, and your code does not change.
- [Prompt store](https://docs.quilrai.dev/llm-gateway/cost-and-traffic/prompt-store.md): Store reusable system prompts centrally, then reference one or more of them and add inline instructions at request time.

### Monitor

- [Agent Monitoring](https://docs.quilrai.dev/llm-gateway/monitor/agent-monitoring.md): Correlate gateway LLM calls with agent runs, traces, workflows, and conversations via W3C/vendor tracing headers, Quilr agent headers, baggage, or provider request-body metadata.
- [Conversation Grouping](https://docs.quilrai.dev/llm-gateway/monitor/conversation-grouping.md): Group gateway requests into conversations with a conversation ID header and see them in Activity.
- [Alerts](https://docs.quilrai.dev/llm-gateway/monitor/alerts.md): App-level and per-provider failure-rate alerts with email and webhook channels.
- [Audit Log](https://docs.quilrai.dev/llm-gateway/monitor/app-audit-log.md): Configuration change history, per-version audit, and rollback for gateway apps.

### Self-service

- [Overview](https://docs.quilrai.dev/llm-gateway/self-service/overview.md): Let developers get gateway access and manage their own keys, without an admin minting a key for every person.
- [Admin Guide](https://docs.quilrai.dev/llm-gateway/self-service/admin-guide.md): For QuilrAI platform admins - choose a credential mode, grant Viewer Access, Settings Request Access, Direct Settings Update, API Key Visibility, and All Logs Visibility, scope each with Everyone/Specific rules, smart groups, and exceptions, review change requests, and revoke access.
- [Developer Guide](https://docs.quilrai.dev/llm-gateway/self-service/developer-guide.md): For developers - sign in to the Self-Service portal, read the app cards, create and revoke named user API keys, call the gateway with them, view your own logs and findings, and submit settings change requests for admin approval.

### API reference

- [Unified Completions](https://docs.quilrai.dev/llm-gateway/api-reference/unified-completions.md): Compatibility details for OpenAI Chat Completions requests translated to provider-native APIs such as Bedrock Converse, Vertex AI Gemini generateContent, and Anthropic Messages, including parameters, messages, tools, structured output, streaming, and unsupported features.
- [LLM Gateway Log Export API](https://docs.quilrai.dev/llm-gateway/api-reference/log-export-api.md): Export single-key or all-apps LLM Gateway request logs as newline-delimited JSON with cursor pagination, a 15-minute export lag, and a 15-day retention window.
- [Management API](https://docs.quilrai.dev/llm-gateway/api-reference/management-api.md): LLM Gateway Management API v1: overview, quick start, authentication and conventions.
- [Apps and credentials API](https://docs.quilrai.dev/llm-gateway/api-reference/apps-and-credentials-api.md): LLM Gateway Management API v1: apps, provider attachments and gateway credentials, with typed inputs and examples.
- [Providers and configuration API](https://docs.quilrai.dev/llm-gateway/api-reference/providers-and-configuration-api.md): LLM Gateway Management API v1: shared providers, model tests, app configuration, catalogs and history, with typed inputs and examples.
- [Prompt Store](https://docs.quilrai.dev/llm-gateway/api-reference/prompts-api.md): Management v1 Prompt Store; tenant-scoped permissions, typed request inputs and examples.
- [QuilrQL behavior](https://docs.quilrai.dev/llm-gateway/api-reference/policy-api.md): Management v1 QuilrQL behavior; new-app model defaults, stored settings and authority boundaries.

### Release notes

- [UX Changelog](https://docs.quilrai.dev/llm-gateway/release-notes/ux-changelog.md): Recent interface improvements - tagging, filtering, and quality-of-life updates.

## MCP Gateway

Give AI agents governed access to tools. Register MCP servers once, decide who can call which tool, and log every call.

- [MCP Gateway overview](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway.md): Landing page with the main tasks and every section of MCP Gateway.

### Get started

- [Introduction to the MCP Gateway](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/get-started/overview.md): The MCP Gateway page in the console - summary tiles, banners, server cards, the workspace tabs and the settings sections.
- [Quick Start](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/get-started/quick-start.md): Set up the MCP Gateway in 4 steps - add an MCP, configure tools and guardrails, connect an agent, and monitor.
- [Architecture](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/get-started/architecture.md): Tool call processing pipeline - Authenticate, Authorize, Scan, Policy, Connect - with auth mediation details.
- [Integration Guide](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/get-started/integration-guide.md): MCP endpoint URLs, client-to-gateway authentication, gateway-to-upstream auth modes, user claims forwarding, and connection examples.
- [OneMCP](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/get-started/onemcp.md): Unified OneMCP endpoint, smart discovery tools, native memory tools, and inline authentication through an in-chat connector card or connection-link fallback.
- [Agent Custom Instructions](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/get-started/agent-instructions.md): Copy-paste custom-instruction text that steers Claude, ChatGPT, and GitHub Copilot to use the OneMCP discovery flow (find_relevant_tools, call_tool, list_mcp_connections), with per-client placement and org-level admin push options and scope caveats.

### Servers and connections

- [Adding MCP Servers](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/servers-and-connections/adding-mcp-servers.md): Add a remote MCP server, choose how the gateway signs in, add custom headers, connect OAuth servers, and install from the MCP Library.
- [MCP Library](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/servers-and-connections/mcp-library.md): Browse and search the MCP Library, filter by status, type and sign-in, install or set up servers, and handle install requests from users.
- [Turn an API into MCP tools](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/servers-and-connections/api-to-mcp.md): Turn a REST API into MCP tools from an OpenAPI spec or as generic HTTP calls, with credentials, access rules and per-operation control.
- [Allowed Agents](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/servers-and-connections/allowed-agents.md): Match AI clients by user-agent keyword, choose which MCP servers each agent can use, and add custom agents.
- [OAuth Connect](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/servers-and-connections/oauth-connect.md): Add OAuth servers, connect them as an administrator, how users connect, and how OAuth passthrough differs.
- [OAuth Permissions](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/servers-and-connections/oauth-permissions.md): Choose which OAuth scopes a server asks users for and see which tools each scope unlocks.
- [API Tokens](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/servers-and-connections/api-tokens.md): Create, use and revoke direct-connection tokens for a server, sent with the mcpuser email header.

### Protect

- [Server access](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/protect/server-access.md): Allow or deny each MCP server by agent, smart group and user, and how those lists take precedence.
- [Group and user rules](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/protect/group-and-user-rules.md): Override tools, confirmation, guardrails and token saving for a smart group or a single user, and preview a user's effective settings.
- [Tool visibility](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/protect/tool-visibility.md): Turn individual tools on or off per server, review read-only, write and destructive tools, and view input schemas.
- [Human approval](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/protect/human-approval.md): Require a person to approve a tool call, optionally with a written justification, and what users see in each AI client.
- [Tool change watch](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/protect/tool-change-watch.md): Get notified when a server adds, removes or changes tools, and approve or dismiss each change.
- [Security guardrails](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/protect/security-guardrails.md): Data risk and adversarial categories on tool arguments and tool results, with Block, Redact, Partial Redact and Monitor actions.
- [Web search security](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/protect/web-search-security.md): Connect Zscaler Internet Access and apply its URL decisions, URL overrides and group domain exclusions to QuilrAI Web Search.
- [Claims forwarding](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/protect/claims-forwarding.md): Forward gateway-generated, versioned user identity to trusted non-OAuth MCP servers in the reserved X-User-Claims header for direct MCP and OneMCP traffic.
- [Input aliases](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/protect/input-aliases.md): Review and apply quick fixes that translate mismatched AI client inputs into the inputs a tool expects.
- [Usage quotas and concurrency](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/protect/usage-quotas-and-concurrency.md): Cap how many tool calls can be made in a time window, and how many can run at the same time. Use quotas to stop a runaway agent or a heavy user from exhausting an MCP server or its upstream API limits.
- [Token saving](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/protect/token-saving.md): Per-server strategies that shorten tool results (smart JSON compression, HTML to text, Markdown to text, text compression) and where savings appear.

### Local MCP

- [Local MCP Overview](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/local-mcp/overview.md): Run administrator-approved Python and Node MCP servers on a user's own computer with every tool call still checked by the gateway - what runs on the user's computer versus the gateway, how it differs from remote OneMCP, prerequisites, and current boundaries (macOS/Linux only, not an OS sandbox, no offline execution).
- [Administrator Setup](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/local-mcp/admin-setup.md): Add a local package (CLI MCP), review its source, runtime, tool schemas and dependency lock, approve the version, then enable tools and configure access, guardrails and group/user rules - including Policy Engine mode, verification before rollout, revoking an installation, and reading Activity tool calls.
- [Build Your Own Package](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/local-mcp/build-a-package.md): Package definition schema for bundled MCP source, package rules and limits (source, tools, Python requirements.lock, Node lockfile v3, environment names, immutable versioning), environment variable handling, Playwright and CLI-wrapper guidance, and designing for serialized execution.
- [Connect Your AI App](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/local-mcp/connect-your-ai-app.md): The one-command user flow for Cursor, Claude Desktop, Claude Code and VS Code - run the version-pinned npm or PyPI connection command, approve the computer in the browser, restart the client, and call a tool. Covers connection states, quilr_connect sign-in, workspace and interpreter flags, and disconnecting.
- [Troubleshooting](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/local-mcp/troubleshooting.md): Symptom table for local packages unavailable, pairing rejection, gateway 401/403, Python version and dependency failures, missing tools and integrity mismatch - plus diagnosing a specific connection with --state, the Preparing response, response-policy blocks, and starting over cleanly.

### Provider setup

- [MCP provider setup](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/provider-setup/overview.md): Set up the provider side of an MCP connection. Most providers need a provider-owned OAuth app with a manual Client ID and Client Secret; a few only need their MCP server URL added manually.
- [Slack](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/provider-setup/slack.md): Create a Slack app, enable Model Context Protocol, add the redirect URL and user-token scopes, and copy the Client ID and Client Secret for manual OAuth.
- [GitHub](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/provider-setup/github.md): Create a GitHub OAuth app, set the callback URL, and copy the Client ID and Client Secret for manual OAuth.
- [Zoho](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/provider-setup/zoho.md): Connect Zoho Cliq MCP - no OAuth app or Client ID/Secret needed; generate the MCP server URL in the Zoho MCP console and add it manually.
- [Datadog](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/provider-setup/datadog.md): Connect Datadog MCP - no OAuth app or Client ID/Secret needed; register the QuilrAI callback URL in Datadog Organization Settings under MCP OAuth Redirect URLs, enable MCP Access and the separate MCP Write Access opt-in, pick the core or toolsets=all endpoint for your Datadog site, and add that endpoint URL manually.
- [Zoom](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/provider-setup/zoom.md): Connect Zoom's remote MCP server - create a Zoom Marketplace General App with user-managed OAuth, add the QuilrAI callback to the redirect URL and allow list, register the granular scopes for the Zoom, Docs, or Whiteboard server, and copy the Client ID and Client Secret for manual OAuth.
- [Excalidraw](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/provider-setup/excalidraw.md): Connect Excalidraw - no OAuth app or Client ID/Secret needed; self-host the community Excalidraw MCP server with its live canvas, bridge stdio to streamable HTTP with Supergateway, and add the resulting /mcp URL manually. Covers all 26 tools, environment variables, and network-security guidance.
- [Asana](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/provider-setup/asana.md): Connect the Asana V2 MCP server (https://mcp.asana.com/v2/mcp) - create an Asana MCP app in the developer console, add the QuilrAI redirect URL, configure workspace distribution, and paste the Client ID and Client Secret into QuilrAI with Auto-detect auth mode. Covers the retired V1 /sse endpoint and workspace-distribution errors.
- [dbt Labs](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/provider-setup/dbt-labs.md): Connect the dbt platform remote MCP server - no OAuth app or Client ID/Secret needed; copy the account-specific MCP Endpoint URL from dbt Account settings > Access URLs, add it manually, and authorize through dbt sign-in plus MFA enrollment. Covers the token-based alternative with Authorization and x-dbt-* headers, PAT vs service token limits, toolset restriction headers, and the remote toolsets (Semantic Layer, Discovery, SQL, Administrative API, Fusion, Product Docs).
- [Netskope](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/provider-setup/netskope.md): Connect the Netskope-hosted MCP server (technology preview, requires a signed Test Evaluation Agreement) - no OAuth app or Client ID/Secret; combine a Netskope-issued 6-character access code in the URL path with a REST API v2 bearer token, format the tenant identifier for multi-region tenants, and allowlist the MCP server egress IPs 184.32.255.197/32 and 52.89.242.156/32. Covers the ~77 tools across events, incidents, policy, users, IPsec, and DNS security, and the write tools that change enforcement configuration.
- [PitchBook](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/provider-setup/pitchbook.md): Connect the PitchBook Premium Connector remote MCP - its Dynamic Client Registration is allowlisted, so confirm licence, SSO, and MCP service access, ask PitchBook to register the QuilrAI callback and return a Client ID and Client Secret (or allowlist the callback for DCR), install from the MCP Library with OAuth credentials or use OAuth passthrough for partner clients, restrict the server to licensed seats with Access Control, and roll out read-only.
- [Salesforce](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/provider-setup/salesforce.md): Connect Salesforce two ways - the Salesforce Hosted MCP servers (activate SObject Reads/Mutations/Deletes/All, create an External Client App with the QuilrAI callback URL, mcp_api and refresh_token scopes, PKCE, refresh token rotation, and JWT-based access tokens, then use the Consumer Key as the Client ID with no secret), or the third-party Cirra (Salesforce MCP) admin server (https://mcp.cirra.ai/mcp) installed from the MCP Library with optional Client ID/Secret left empty, authorized by signing in with a Salesforce account. Covers sandbox URLs and troubleshooting.

### Quilr-provided MCPs

- [Quilr-Provided MCPs](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/quilr-provided-mcps/overview.md): Compare Quilr-built and operated MCP integrations by use case, capabilities, connection method, and whether their tool surface can change provider data.
- [Official MCP Comparison](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/quilr-provided-mcps/official-comparison.md): Provider-by-provider comparison of official MCP or API coverage with Quilr's custom tool surface, operating model, safety controls, compound tools, and known limits.
- [Microsoft 365 v3](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/quilr-provided-mcps/microsoft-365-v3.md): Flagship unified Microsoft 365 MCP for Outlook mail and calendar, OneDrive, SharePoint, Teams, directory, OneNote, cross-workload search, batch operations, and delta sync, including a capability comparison with ChatGPT Outlook and SharePoint connectors.
- [SharePoint](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/quilr-provided-mcps/sharepoint.md): Six consolidated tools for SharePoint sites, drives, files, folders, lists, list items, URL resolution, controlled writes, and confirmed deletes.
- [Excel](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/quilr-provided-mcps/excel.md): Eight workbook dispatchers covering worksheets, ranges, formulas, formatting, tables, named ranges, charts, pivots, and function evaluation.
- [Microsoft Tasks & Planner](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/quilr-provided-mcps/microsoft-tasks-planner.md): Focused Microsoft To Do and Planner tools for personal tasks, plans, buckets, and team tasks.
- [Azure DevOps Advanced](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/quilr-provided-mcps/azure-devops.md): Azure DevOps Advanced is a Quilr-built MCP for Azure DevOps Services (dev.azure.com). It provides 47 tools across organizations, projects, Azure Repos, pull requests, Boards, Pipelines, Test Plans, Wiki, Search and...
- [Jira](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/quilr-provided-mcps/jira.md): Compact ten-tool Jira surface for projects, issue retrieval and search, creation, assignment, transitions, and comments.
- [Confluence](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/quilr-provided-mcps/confluence.md): Nine-tool Confluence surface for spaces, pages, CQL search, page creation and updates, and comments with no destructive tools.
- [Google Workspace](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/quilr-provided-mcps/google-workspace.md): Google Workspace is a Quilr-built MCP in the Library for Gmail, Google Calendar, Google Drive and Workspace directory lookups. There is no shared Quilr-owned Google client: each tenant connects with its own Google...
- [Figma](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/quilr-provided-mcps/figma.md): Figma is a Quilr-built MCP in the Library for design context, comments and Code Connect. There is no shared Quilr-owned Figma app: each tenant connects with its own Figma OAuth app, which keeps tenants isolated.
- [Calendly](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/quilr-provided-mcps/calendly.md): The Quilr-built Calendly MCP connects with a Calendly OAuth application that your organization owns. A Calendly administrator creates the application and gives its Client ID and Client Secret to the MCP Gateway. Each...
- [HubSpot CRM](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/quilr-provided-mcps/hubspot.md): Nine consolidated tools for CRM search, batch reads, associations, schemas, owners, records, notes, tasks, and controlled archive.
- [Avoma](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/quilr-provided-mcps/avoma.md): Four read-only meeting-intelligence tools for meeting details, transcripts, and structured notes.
- [Writer](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/quilr-provided-mcps/writer.md): Hosted ten-tool Writer surface for chat, applications, Knowledge Graphs, files, translation, vision, and web search.
- [Optimizely Experimentation](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/quilr-provided-mcps/optimizely.md): Quilr-built experimentation MCP for schema-guided queries, reporting, entity lifecycle, exports, audit history, collaborators, and datafiles.
- [Semrush Advanced](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/quilr-provided-mcps/semrush.md): Semrush Advanced is a Quilr-built MCP for SEO, keyword, backlink, traffic, market and project research. It signs in with a Semrush API key, not an OAuth app.
- [BrowserStack Advanced](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/quilr-provided-mcps/browserstack.md): BrowserStack Advanced is a Quilr-built MCP for BrowserStack account discovery, browser and device inventories, Automate and App Automate sessions, diagnostics, app uploads and Test Management. It signs in with a...
- [Athenahealth](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/quilr-provided-mcps/athenahealth.md): Safety-first athenaOne and FHIR MCP with capability packs, allowlists, idempotent confirmed writes, separately enabled deletes, bulk exports, and PHI-safe telemetry.
- [Tavily](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/quilr-provided-mcps/tavily.md): Eight read-only tools for search, extraction, site mapping, crawling, asynchronous research, usage, and key information.
- [Cycode](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/quilr-provided-mcps/cycode.md): Remotely operated Cycode CLI MCP wrapper for service status and secret scanning without general shell access.
- [Quilr Web Search](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/quilr-provided-mcps/web-search.md): Minimal two-tool web search and webpage retrieval integration with optional gateway domain policy.
- [SketchIt](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/quilr-provided-mcps/sketchit.md): SketchIt is a Quilr-built MCP that turns a description of a process, structure or dataset into a rendered diagram or chart. It has no upstream service and no credential: it makes no API calls, no LLM calls and...
- [PDF Editor](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/quilr-provided-mcps/pdf-editor.md): PDF Editor is a Quilr-built MCP that reads, searches and edits PDF documents, including scanned ones, and hands back a finished file. There is no OAuth app, client ID, client secret or API key: PDF Editor is enabled,...

### API reference

- [MCP Gateway Log Export API](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/api-reference/log-export-api.md): Export server-scoped or tenant-scoped MCP tool call logs as newline-delimited JSON with cursor pagination, a 15-minute export lag, and a 15-day retention window.

## Red Teaming

Test gateway apps, agents, models and MCP servers against real attack techniques, then fix what breaks with hardened prompts and new detections.

- [Red Teaming overview](https://docs.quilrai.dev/red-teaming.md): Landing page with the main tasks and every section of Red Teaming.

### Get started

- [Red Teaming overview](https://docs.quilrai.dev/red-teaming/get-started/overview.md): Red Teaming actively tests your LLM apps, MCP servers, agents, and models for weaknesses before attackers find them. It lives in the console under Assessments.
- [Reading a report](https://docs.quilrai.dev/red-teaming/get-started/reading-a-report.md): Each Red Teaming tool produces its own kind of result. This page explains how to read each one, in the order that tells you what to fix first.

### Assessments

- [LLM Intelligence Assessment](https://docs.quilrai.dev/red-teaming/assessments/llm-intelligence-assessment.md): Benchmark the model behind an app against fixed adversarial and capability suites. Covers simulating your app with a system prompt and tool schemas, the Guardian counterfactual, and compliance framework rollups.
- [MCP Threat Detection](https://docs.quilrai.dev/red-teaming/assessments/mcp-threat-detection.md): Vet any MCP server before you trust it. MCP Threat Detection is a supply-chain check: it scans an MCP server's code and dependencies and enumerates what the server exposes, then builds a threat model from the results.
- [Agentic Red Teaming](https://docs.quilrai.dev/red-teaming/assessments/agentic-red-teaming.md): Multi-turn adversarial assessment of a live AI agent over HTTP or voice - connect, choose attack coverage (Quick scan, Full library, Select attacks, custom objectives), and launch with an evaluation policy.
- [Model Red Teaming](https://docs.quilrai.dev/red-teaming/assessments/model-red-teaming.md): Red team one model or compare 2-8 models side by side, from your gateway models, QuilrAI-provided models, or manual entry, with system prompts and Tool Studio.

### Operate

- [Red Team Findings and Schedules](https://docs.quilrai.dev/red-teaming/operate/runs-findings-and-schedules.md): Track findings through review statuses with an audit history, and schedule recurring assessments.
- [Red Team Attack Library](https://docs.quilrai.dev/red-teaming/operate/attack-library.md): All 64 attack objectives by OWASP category with MITRE ATLAS technique, severity, and Quick scan membership.
- [Turn findings into detections](https://docs.quilrai.dev/red-teaming/operate/turn-findings-into-detections.md): Agentic and Model Red Teaming reports do more than list what broke. The Remediation section of each report suggests controls that would stop the same attacks in production. This page explains where each suggestion goes.

## Browser Extension

See which AI apps people use in the browser, stop sensitive data at the prompt, and guide users at the moment they need it.

- [Browser Extension overview](https://docs.quilrai.dev/browser-extension.md): Landing page with the main tasks and every section of Browser Extension.

### Get started

- [Browser Extension overview](https://docs.quilrai.dev/browser-extension/get-started/overview.md): The QuilrAI Browser Extension governs how people use AI in the browser. It runs in managed Chrome and Edge browsers, together with a small native component (the Browser Agent) that handles device-level tasks the...
- [Deployment prerequisites](https://docs.quilrai.dev/browser-extension/get-started/prerequisites.md): Tenant configuration, enterprise prerequisites, deployment choices, and the Endpoint Agent package boundary.

### Deploy

- [Deploy with Microsoft Intune](https://docs.quilrai.dev/browser-extension/deploy/microsoft-intune.md): Deploy Windows and macOS Browser Agent packages and tenant-specific browser extension profiles with Intune.
- [Deploy with Jamf Pro](https://docs.quilrai.dev/browser-extension/deploy/jamf-pro.md): Deploy the macOS Browser Agent, Full Disk Access profile, tenant configuration, and browser extension with Jamf Pro.
- [Deploy with Group Policy](https://docs.quilrai.dev/browser-extension/deploy/group-policy.md): Force-install the Browser Extension and deploy its native Browser Agent through a computer-linked Windows GPO.
- [Validate deployment](https://docs.quilrai.dev/browser-extension/deploy/validate-deployment.md): Verify management assignment, browser policy, native processes, console registration, and synthetic telemetry independently.

### Configure

- [Extension settings](https://docs.quilrai.dev/browser-extension/configure/extension-settings.md): Tenant-wide settings for the Browser Extension live in the console under Settings › Browser Extension. The page has two tabs: Deployment Management (this page) and Whitelist Domain & Pattern (see Allowed domains and...
- [Allowed domains and patterns](https://docs.quilrai.dev/browser-extension/configure/allowed-domains-and-patterns.md): Use the allowlist to exclude trusted sites, such as internal tools, from Browser Extension monitoring. It lives on the Whitelist Domain & Pattern tab of the Browser Extension settings.
- [Browser controls](https://docs.quilrai.dev/browser-extension/configure/browser-controls.md): A browser control tells the extension what to watch for and what to do when it happens, for example "a user shares sensitive data with an AI application". Controls live on the Browser Extension tab of the Policy...

### Capabilities

- [Clipboard monitoring](https://docs.quilrai.dev/browser-extension/capabilities/clipboard-monitoring.md): Clipboard monitoring catches sensitive data at the copy step. The QuilrAI agent on the endpoint watches clipboard events, sends them to the Browser Extension for a DLP decision, and then allows the copy, clears the...
- [File indexing](https://docs.quilrai.dev/browser-extension/capabilities/file-indexing.md): File indexing keeps a local index of files on the endpoint so the DLP engine can quickly resolve the real file behind an upload or download and scan it. The QuilrAI agent builds the index from paths you configure,...
- [Agent kill switch (extension)](https://docs.quilrai.dev/browser-extension/capabilities/agent-kill-switch.md): The Browser Extension can switch off the QuilrAI agent on the endpoint and switch it back on, without restarting any process. While disabled, the agent stops its services (clipboard monitoring and file indexing) and...

## Endpoint Agent

See and govern AI on company devices: desktop chat apps, coding agents, local models and the MCP servers they run.

- [Endpoint Agent overview](https://docs.quilrai.dev/endpoint-agent.md): Landing page with the main tasks and every section of Endpoint Agent.

### Get started

- [Endpoint Agent overview](https://docs.quilrai.dev/endpoint-agent/get-started/overview.md): The QuilrAI Endpoint Agent discovers and governs AI use that happens outside the browser: desktop AI apps, coding agents, local models, and the MCP servers and skills they use. It runs as a background service on...
- [Requirements](https://docs.quilrai.dev/endpoint-agent/get-started/requirements.md): Check that your endpoints meet these requirements before you deploy the QuilrAI Endpoint Agent.

### Configure

- [Agent settings](https://docs.quilrai.dev/endpoint-agent/configure/agent-settings.md): Tenant-wide Endpoint Agent behavior is set on one page in the console. These settings apply to every enrolled workstation. Per-app detection and enforcement rules are set separately in App policies.
- [App policies](https://docs.quilrai.dev/endpoint-agent/configure/app-policies.md): App policies decide how the Endpoint Agent detects and acts on sensitive data in each AI application. They live on the Endpoint Agent tab of the Policy Engine. For how the Policy Engine works across surfaces, see...

### How it works

- [Network monitoring](https://docs.quilrai.dev/endpoint-agent/how-it-works/network-monitoring.md): The Endpoint Agent's network monitor is a local proxy that inspects AI traffic leaving the device. It decrypts HTTPS with a locally trusted certificate, runs DLP on requests and responses, and allows, blocks, or asks...
- [Process mapping](https://docs.quilrai.dev/endpoint-agent/how-it-works/process-mapping.md): Process mapping is how the Endpoint Agent builds an inventory of applications and AI components on each device, ties running processes to those applications, and enforces execution policies. It starts discovery as...
- [Backend connectivity](https://docs.quilrai.dev/endpoint-agent/how-it-works/backend-connectivity.md): The Endpoint Agent talks to the QuilrAI backend over outbound HTTPS only. It pushes what it discovers, pulls governance decisions, and reports enforcement activity.

### Deploy and operate

- [Deployment and status](https://docs.quilrai.dev/endpoint-agent/deploy-and-operate/deployment-and-status.md): Roll the Endpoint Agent out to your fleet, then use the console to track coverage and switch individual workstations on or off.
- [Agent kill switch](https://docs.quilrai.dev/endpoint-agent/deploy-and-operate/agent-kill-switch.md): Use the kill switch to stop the Endpoint Agent on one device or across your tenant, for example if it interferes with users' work, and to restore it afterwards. No reinstall or new package is needed.

## Integrations

Pull AI usage from SaaS and agent platforms into QuilrAI, and send findings and audit events to your SIEM.

- [Integrations overview](https://docs.quilrai.dev/integrations.md): Landing page with the main tasks and every section of Integrations.

### Get started

- [How integrations work](https://docs.quilrai.dev/integrations/get-started/how-integrations-work.md): Integrations connect third-party platforms to QuilrAI. Some bring AI usage, inventory, and compliance data into Quilr; others send Quilr activity, findings, and alerts from Quilr to your security and operations tools.

### Pull AI usage and inventory

- [Claude Compliance API](https://docs.quilrai.dev/integrations/pull-ai-usage-and-inventory/claude-compliance-api.md): The Claude Compliance integration gives your organization visibility into Claude.ai usage through Anthropic's Compliance API. After you register a Compliance API key, Quilr continuously fetches your organization's...
- [OpenAI Compliance](https://docs.quilrai.dev/integrations/pull-ai-usage-and-inventory/openai-compliance.md): The OpenAI Compliance integration brings OpenAI organization compliance events and governed inventory into Quilr, so ChatGPT workspace activity shows up next to the activity your sensors capture.
- [Microsoft Copilot Studio](https://docs.quilrai.dev/integrations/pull-ai-usage-and-inventory/microsoft-copilot-studio.md): Connect Microsoft Copilot Studio external threat detection to QuilrAI guardrails before tool execution.
- [Azure AI Foundry](https://docs.quilrai.dev/integrations/pull-ai-usage-and-inventory/azure-ai-foundry.md): The Azure AI Foundry integration discovers agents, projects, models, access, and governed activity in your Azure subscriptions. The connector performs read-only discovery and monitoring; it does not perform Foundry...
- [GitHub](https://docs.quilrai.dev/integrations/pull-ai-usage-and-inventory/github.md): The GitHub integration discovers repositories, AI projects, workflows, and related developer inventory, so you can see where AI is used in your engineering estate.
- [TrueFoundry](https://docs.quilrai.dev/integrations/pull-ai-usage-and-inventory/truefoundry.md): Use QuilrAI SDK checks as TrueFoundry custom input/output guardrails, including Mutate and Bearer setup, rail selectors, full request/response examples, streaming requirements, verification, identity, and fail-open behavior.

### Send logs and alerts

- [Syslog](https://docs.quilrai.dev/integrations/send-logs-and-alerts/syslog.md): Forwards the Extension findings to your syslog server based on the controls configured.
- [Syslog Audit](https://docs.quilrai.dev/integrations/send-logs-and-alerts/syslog-audit-events.md): Forwards audit log events to your syslog server. Supports optional filtering to control which audit events are delivered.
- [Webhook](https://docs.quilrai.dev/integrations/send-logs-and-alerts/webhook.md): Forwards Extension findings and audit log events to your webhook endpoint.
- [Microsoft Sentinel](https://docs.quilrai.dev/integrations/send-logs-and-alerts/microsoft-sentinel.md): The Microsoft Sentinel integration sends Quilr activity and findings into a Sentinel security workspace, so your SOC can investigate AI risk alongside other security events.
